Interpret bx<ax+4 as asking for the x-values where the y-value of the line y=bx is below the y-value of the line y=ax+4. From the graph, to the left of their intersection A, the y=bx line lies below the y=ax+4 line; to the right, it lies above. Since the intersection x-coordinate is 1, the solution is x<1.

Since A lies on y=bx, substitute (1,3): 3=b, so b=3. Since A lies on y=ax+4, substitute (1,3): 3=a+4, so a=-1. The inequality becomes 3x<-x+4, hence 4x<4, so x<1.
